caveats: Smoothers, not deployable models: both sides drop lag_yield and the year RE, so neither LOYO RMSE reflects the project's deployable model performance.
fPLS is supervised dimension reduction; the Bayesian model is an unsupervised RW2 smoothness prior on a fixed 5-basis reduction — different estimator classes, not two settings of one knob.
fpls_component_selection is selection-optimistic (k chosen to minimize the same score reported) and is NOT used to choose the headline model; the headline k is fixed a priori.
The headline RMSE comparison (k=1 fPLS vs. 5-basis RW2 Bayesian) is confounded by a flexibility asymmetry, not just fold count — do not read the RMSE gap as 'which method is better.'
~9 LOYO folds means pooled RMSE is a noisy, underpowered estimator; the beta(t) shape overlay (primary result) is more informative than the RMSE table (secondary diagnostic).
